newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian grain industry head sees no major imports.
newsitem.headline: Russian grain industry head sees no major imports.

text.p: The head of one of Russia's leading grain trade agencies, Roskhleboprodukt, was quoted by Interfax news agency on Friday as saying that he saw no reason for Russia to make major grain imports.
Leonid Cheshinsky said he saw 1996 net grain output at 70 million tonnes, with losses due to bad weather, including drought in the Northern Caucasus and rains in Siberia, at five million tonnes.
But he said he saw net wheat output at 36-38 million tonnes -- far above last year's official 30.1 million tonnes and above independent analysts' predictions of 33-35 million tonnes.
Cheshinsky, president of the semi-state run Roskhleboprodukt, was quoted as saying that "quality" grain would comprise only 10 percent of the wheat crop.
"But there is no need for Russia to make major grain imports," he was quoted as saying.
Cheshinsky's overall output estimates are in line with those of private-sector analysts, who see Russian net grain output this year unlikely to reach levels forecast by the government.
But analysts and officials have said Russia will continue to import grains.

Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha, in charge of the harvest, said this week that he saw the 1996 net grain harvest at up to 72 million tonnes. Prime Minister Vivktor Chernomyrdin told parliament he saw net output at 77-78 million tonnes.
Cheshinsky said the low quality harvest would not affect the amount of bread and flour Russia would produce.

Officials are having trouble gauging output because farmers may be underreporting, he said, adding that last year's official net harvest of 63.4 million tonnes may have in fact been three million tonnes higher.
Still, Russia is facing one of its worst harvests in three decades and its second low harvest in a row.
